Blue Letter Bible study tools make reading, searching and studying the Bible easy and rewarding.

passages.title: Ps. 36:1–4
passages.text: The **wicked** person has **no fear of God before his eyes** (see Rom. 3:18 ). He does evil and plans evil. He particularly schemes to bring trouble to others, especially the godly.

passages.title: Ps. 36:5–9
passages.text: The pairing of God’s **steadfast love** and **faithfulness** recalls Ex. 34:6 , describing God’s kindness. **Righteousness** and **judgments** express God’s enduring commitment to act kindly toward his creatures and to **save** them. In view of this, people can **take refuge** under his **wings** and can be welcome guests at his table.

passages.title: Ps. 36:10–12
passages.text: The psalm ends with an appeal to God’s reliable love for his faithful ones (**those who know you**, that is, **the upright of heart**).

notes.text: **Psalm** . This is a lament that reflects on the wicked and on the steadfast love of the Lord. It concludes with a prayer that God will protect his people from the attacks of the wicked.
The **fountain of life** refreshes and sustains life; see Prov. 10:11 ; 13:14 . To **see light** means to experience life (e.g., Job 33:28 ; Ps. 49:19 ).
